questions.question: VSEPR predicts an SbF 5 molecule will be which of the following shapes?
questions.explanation: The Lewis (electron-dot) structure has five bonding pairs around the central Sb and no lone pairs. VSEPR predicts this number of pairs to give a trigonal bipyramidal structure.

questions.question: The shortest bond would be present in which of the following substances?
questions.explanation: All the bonds except in CO are single bonds. The CO bond is a triple bond. Triple bonds are shorter than double bonds, which are shorter than single bonds. Drawing Lewis structures might help you answer this question.

questions.question: Which of the following does not have one or more π bonds?
questions.explanation: Answers B through D contain molecules or ions with double or triple bonds. Double and triple bonds contain π bonds. Water has only single ( σ ) bonds. If any of these are not obvious to you, draw a Lewis structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is polar?
questions.explanation: The VSEPR model predicts all the other molecules to be nonpolar.

questions.question: Resonance structures are necessary to describe the bonding in which of the following?
questions.explanation: All the other answers involve species containing only single bonds. Substances without double or triple bonds seldom need resonance structures.

questions.question: An explanation of the equivalent bond lengths of the nitrite ion is:
questions.explanation: Resonance causes bonds to have the same average length.

questions.question: Most organic substances have low melting points. This may be because, in most cases, the intermolecular forces are:
questions.explanation: Many organic molecules are nonpolar. Nonpolar substances are held together by weak van der Waals attractions.

questions.question: Which of the following has more than one unshared pair of valence electrons on the central atom?
questions.explanation: Lewis structures are required. You do not need to draw all of them. A and B have one unshared pair, while C does not have an unshared pair. D has two unshared pairs of electrons.

questions.question: What is the expected hybridization of the central atom in a molecule of TiCl 4? This molecule is tetrahedral.
questions.explanation: Tetrahedral molecules are normally sp 3 hybridized.

questions.question: The only substance listed below that contains ionic, σ, and π bonds is:
questions.explanation: Only A and D are ionic. The chloride ion has no internal bonds, so σ and π bonds are not possible.

questions.question: The electron pairs point toward the corners of which geometrical shape for a molecule with sp 2 hybrid orbitals?
questions.explanation: This hybridization requires a geometrical shape with three corners.

questions.question: Regular tetrahedral molecules or ions include which of the following?
questions.explanation: One or more Lewis structures may help you. A is an irregular tetrahedron (seesaw); C and D are square planar.

questions.question: Which molecule or ion in the following list has the greatest number of unshared electrons around the central atom?
questions.explanation: A has 0. B has 2. C and D have 0. You may need to draw one or more Lewis structures.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules is the least polar?
questions.explanation: All the molecules are polar except B.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules is the most polar?
questions.explanation: Drawing one or more Lewis structures may help you. Only A and C are polar. Only the ammonia has hydrogen bonding, which is very, very polar.

questions.question: Which of the following processes involves breaking an ionic bond?
questions.explanation: C is breaking metallic bonding. All the others involve covalently bonded molecules.
